rationale: The Latin anchors falx (sickle/scythe), marra (hoe/mattock), falcastrum (pruning hook), and ensis curvus (curved sword) all point to a curved cutting implement. The Old English BIL is consistently used in heroic poetry (Beowulf, Caedmon) as a bladed weapon or tool, and bill.n.08 — a long-handled saw/tool with a curved blade — is the closest WordNet synset to this sense of a curved cutting implement.
